ven’t met for almost the entire duration of your second term as vice chair. One of the major drawback of these e-meetings is that “saying goodbye” through NWM is not very warm… though the best we can do!. So I hope having the chance meeting with you again soon. Wish you all the best !! Have a great future without chairing RAN1 sessions. Warm regards - Patrick 146 – Apple France Thank you Havish for your dedication and excellent management as RAN1 vice-chair, especially for chairing Rel-17 ePos. Best Regards-Ali 147 – Ericsson India Private Limited Thank you Havish for your technical contributions to 3GPP and for your excellent leadership for the last four years in RAN1. Wish you all the best for your future role, and hope we can have a proper RAN1 farewell in person sometime very soon. 148 – Ericsson India Private Limited Thank you Havish for your technical contributions to 3GPP and for your excellent leadership for the last four years in RAN1. Wish you all the best for your future role, and hope we can have a proper RAN1 farewell in person sometime very soon. BR Ajit 149 – Apple Europe Limited Hi Havish, Did not have many opportunities to sit in the sessions you chaired because of the topics I have been tracking. But whenever I did, I was always impressed by how you gave every delegate a chance to voice his/her view and at the same time encouraged delegates to reach agreements/compromises respectfully, which has been well known about you from LAA/eLAA days. Really appreciate your great service to RAN1! Best regards, Weidong 150 – China Telecommunications Hi Havish, Thank you for your excellent leadership as RAN1 VC for the past 4 years. Wish you all the best in the future! Best regards, Jianchi Zhu (China Telecom) 151 – WILUS Inc. Thank you Havish for leading RAN1 with your great leadership as vice-chair for the past 4 years. I will never forget your passion for leading technical discussions from when you were charing as a WI rappateure to beyond mid-night.^^It’s been really pleasure to work with you in RAN1. Wish you all the best. - Minseok 152 – Samsung Research America Dear Havish, Thank you for all your great contributions to RAN1 as vice-chair/rapporteur/delegate. I admire your consistent way of handling discussions no matter whether chairing a controversial topic, handling a persistent delegate, discussing offline or in a 1-to-1 conversation – always with respect, kindness, patience, a smile and insightful technical views. Will miss you :) and I do hope you continue working in 3GPP. Best wishes!! Warm regards, Carmela

Hope you will continue RAN1 work and meet you soon in RAN1. Yingyang (Intel) 158 – Panasonic Corporation Thank you Havish for your hard work and excellent leadership! Wish you all the best. Nishio (Panasonic) 159 – Sony Europe B.V. Thank you Havish for your leadership and significant contribution to RAN1 in the last 4 years as VC. Your patient, high technical skills, toughness, and fairness are the key success of NR positioning. :-) I wish you success for your future endeavors and do hope to see each other when the pandemic is ended. /Basuki - SONY 160 – MediaTek Inc. Dear Havish, Thanks for your great patience and contribution to RAN1, and it’s my great honor to join your session and work with you! Wish you all the best! Xuanbo (MediaTek) 161 – Nokia Shanghai Bell Dear Havish, Thank you for your great effort as a great RAN1 VC! Your calm and effectively pushing on the progress is really helpful for the topics and releases, especially some time with many different opinions from companies. Wish you all the best in the future! Best Regards, Jingyuan 162 – BBC Dear Havish, thank you very much for all your work, for your kind approach and patience during all the difficult discussions. I wish you all the best in your future. With best regards, David. 163 – Nokia Japan Thank you Havish for your excellent leadership and dedication. It was an great honor for me to work over the last years for Rel-16/17 NR positioning. Thank you for very good chairing and wish you all the best ! -Hyunsu (Nokia) 164 – Ericsson LM Thank you Havish for showing excellent leadership and patience with us! You have set the standards high for how to chair these technical meetings. - Narendar 165 – ZTE Corporation Dear Havish, thank you very much for your excellent contribution and leadership, starting from LTE LAA and then various topics for 5G NR! Your professionalism certainly has gained a lot of respect and appreciation from delegates including me. Wish you all the best in your future endeavors! Hope I will have opportunities to work with you again and look forward to meeting each other in the near future! - Ruyue (ZTE) 166 – Ericsson Inc. Thank you Havish for your excellent contributions, leadership and all the great discussions in RAN1. Good luck for your future endeavors! - Ravi 167 – Motorola Mobility Germany GmbH Hi Havish, Thank you for your dedication and thoughtful leadership, especially as a RAN1 VC. Your ability to be patient and project an aura of calm given the nature and challenge of 3GPP discussions will be greatly missed. Best wishes! - Robin (Lenovo, Motorola Mobility) 168 – Ericsson LM There are plenty of smart and hard working people in 3GPP, but few that have your civility and kindness, especially while chairing the contentious mob that can be a RAN1 meeting. You’ve set a gold standard that I expect 3GPP leaders will draw from for years to come. Best wishes for your future endeavors! -mark 169 – Futurewei Thank you for your great service to the industry. Your leadership was invaluable for leading us forward with some very difficult decisions. I wish you the best for your future endeavours. A (Futurewei) 170 – DENSO CORPORATION It was indeed great effort and achievement for leading RAN1 to produce the high quality standard to drive 5G market. Prefer to discuss the necessity of larger quantization step before we discuss the detail. Sharp | Support. And suggest removing the Y=3. Noted that the current L1 differential RSRP ranges from 0 to -30dB. If we follow the current value range and use the Y=3, we still require 4 bits, as same as the legacy 2dB step, to represent the 10 combination. Futurewei | Not support. Legacy quantization step works well and we don’t see the need of adding new ones. Lenovo | Do not support. We share similar view with OPPO. Apple | Low priority Kyocera | Similar view as OPPO Table 62: Companies | View FL | Most of companies support data collection via L1. There is clear motivation for quantization step relaxation base on SI output. Why not? ZTE | Generally fine. For the first sub-bullet, we prefer to only keep 4dB for Y. 4dB quantization resolution for the reporting of differential RSRP is more generally be used by companies during R18 evaluations. Besides, with Y=4dB, the differential RSRP can be quantized to a 3-bit value and one bit can be saved for the reporting of each differential RSRP. While for 3dB quantization resolution, there’s no such benefit i.e., still 4 bits are needed. For the last note, the benefit of enhancements for the reporting of absolute RSRP is marginal and evaluation verification is deficient. HW/HiSi | Not support. For inference, the L1-RSRP report can be used for multiple purposes in a UE transparent manner, even including legacy operations. Changing the quantization level to a coarser value may impact the performance of these operations (such as scheduling, or pairing) in a negative manner. Also, when Set B is different from Set A, it may be difficult to identify the proper narrow beam direction, since the same quantization level may correspond to a multitude of beams. For training, the overhead is not a large issue anyway since the training data collection is non-real time. As the sole purpose of changing the quantization granularity and range would be an optimization for overhead reduction, this enhancement may not be essential for training data collection either. If the adaptive number is adopted, the field indicating the number of beams needs to be reported additionally. Considering the large specification impacts and unclear gain, we think the following already agreed beam reporting is sufficient for inference results reporting in NW side model. New H3C | OK in general TCL | Agree Xiaomi | Support ZTE | Support. Legacy quantization step works well and we don’t see the need of adding new ones. Lenovo | Do not support. We share similar view with OPPO. Apple | Low priority Kyocera | Similar view as OPPO Table 53: Companies | View FL | Most of companies support data collection via L1. There is clear motivation for quantization step relaxation base on SI output. Why not? ZTE | Generally fine. For the first sub-bullet, we prefer to only keep 4dB for Y. 4dB quantization resolution for the reporting of differential RSRP is more generally be used by companies during R18 evaluations. Besides, with Y=4dB, the differential RSRP can be quantized to a 3-bit value and one bit can be saved for the reporting of each differential RSRP. While for 3dB quantization resolution, there’s no such benefit i.e., still 4 bits are needed. For the last note, the benefit of enhancements for the reporting of absolute RSRP is marginal and evaluation verification is deficient. HW/HiSi | Not support. For inference, the L1-RSRP report can be used for multiple purposes in a UE transparent manner, even including legacy operations. Changing the quantization level to a coarser value may impact the performance of these operations (such as scheduling, or pairing) in a negative manner. Also, when Set B is different from Set A, it may be difficult to identify the proper narrow beam direction, since the same quantization level may correspond to a multitude of beams. For training, the overhead is not a large issue anyway since the training data collection is non-real time. As the sole purpose of changing the quantization granularity and range would be an optimization for overhead reduction, this enhancement may not be essential for training data collection either. Considering the large specification impacts and unclear gain, we think the following already agreed beam reporting is sufficient for inference results reporting in NW side model. New H3C | OK in general TCL | Agree Xiaomi | Support ZTE | Support. FFS: whether/how to report number of reported beams Qualcomm | Share similar view as Docomo. InterDigital | Support.
